finding: Serialization does converge on one site: a static scan finds no second hand-built problem dict anywhere under harness/, and raising every row of every registry in one process shows 121 conditions across 27 boundaries all rendering through the single render_body(), which is the aligned anchor's first clause. The second clause fails when measured: a bound component that raises an untyped exception is re-raised rather than mapped, so it reaches the caller as a bare Python exception with no typed body, and the vocabulary is not closed either, since 24 of the 34 suffixes the harness registries emit have no row in the registry the platform publishes.
gap: No shared-path fallback that converts an unrecognised adapter exception into adapter-unavailable: the run path does getattr(exc, 'body', None) and re-raises when there is none, so the guarantee holds only for components that already type their own failures. And the published closed registry (10 rows) is not reconciled with what the code emits (34 suffixes), including a duplicate spelling of the same fault at a different status.

finding: Nothing recovers by parsing prose and nothing hands a failure to a model to interpret, and an unrecognised type is refused at construction rather than guessed at, so the misaligned anchor is avoided. But the typed failure is not yet the currency of recovery: retryable and retry_after_s are written on every body and read to decide in exactly one place, the failure capability's own demonstration caller, while the real reactions are selected by counters and declared bounds rather than by the failure's type, with escalation fixed as a constant on the loop specification and fired by the permitted attempts being spent.
gap: There is no mapping from problem type to reaction anywhere: retry, escalation and abandonment are chosen from attempt and iteration counts, so two different failure types with the same attempt count get the same reaction and the retryable member that a caller is told to branch on steers nothing inside the platform. Compensation is likewise selected from a declared irreversibility class, not from the failure that occurred.
